problem: Active semantic mapping methods are built and evaluated indoors, where objects have similar scales and viewing distances. They fail to handle urban scenes, where object scale and viewing distance are badly mismatched (unreliable VLM likelihoods) and different object sizes need different mapping behaviours; there is also no urban dataset with object-level annotations.
motivation: Accurate full-scene semantic mapping is needed for frontier-based outdoor navigation. In cities, small objects viewed from far away and large objects viewed up close give poor VLM likelihoods. A single shared value estimator cannot model the heterogeneous strategies needed for pedestrians versus buildings.
key_idea: Train an RL mapping agent that adds a category-aware likelihood-calibration policy alongside the motion policy, decouples the two with a CLUB mutual-information regularizer, and uses per-category value heads balanced by Nash-MTL Pareto optimization.
insight: Ablations show that multi-value heads without gradient balancing collapse (OCR 78.7, Var 433.9). Adding Pareto optimization restores them (OCR 96.5, Var 10.4), and MI further gives the best result (OCR 97.6, Var 8.4). Learned calibration beats every fixed likelihood scale (GLEAM-x, best OCR 91.9 versus 94.7 for LC+MI). MI reduces mean CCA between the motion and calibration features by 27.85% while max CCA stays near 1, so it suppresses shortcut coupling without decorrelating the features.
method: Urban dataset: 80 scenes with GIS/OSM layouts (CityEngine), LLM-planned block semantics and object distributions, rendered in Isaac Sim RTX with varied lighting; object volumes range 0.01 to 208.47k m³ and instance-level annotations are provided.

Likelihood calibration policy: predicts a per-voxel, per-category coefficient β (discrete, 0.2 to 1.8) that scales the raw VLM logits in the softmax before the binary log-odds Bayesian map update; the VLM (CLIP or DINOv3 dino.txt) is not fine-tuned.
Shared encoder with two branches: takes historical poses plus the previous global map and current observation map, and outputs the motion feature Z_α and the calibration feature Z_β.

MI dependence regularizer: a CLUB estimator (Gaussian conditional q(Z_β|Z_α), 256-to-128 MLP, 3 estimator steps per update) penalizes the joint-minus-marginal log-likelihood gap; it acts as a weighted Lagrangian term (k=0.1) and is discarded at inference.
Category-wise value heads: the coverage reward is split per class (small/medium/large by volume), each class gets its own value head and GAE advantage, and the loss is PPO per class plus (k/C)·L_MI.
Pareto optimization: Nash-MTL bargaining weights (GᵀGα=1/α) combine the per-category gradients so no single object scale dominates.
Training: PPO from scratch with a three-layer ResNet, batch size 256, lr 1e-4, 10^3 episodes, about 19 h on one RTX 4090.

setting.backbone: three-layer ResNet encoder trained from scratch with PPO; CLIP or DINOv3 (dino.txt) frozen as the likelihood extractor
setting.training_data: 16 simulated urban scenes (4 validation); 10^3 PPO episodes; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose history, VLM likelihoods projected to a 2D semantic map
setting.action_space: discrete motion actions for viewpoint selection (max 384 steps) plus discrete calibration coefficients
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (custom urban dataset); UrbanBIS reconstructed meshes for transfer
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT semantic map used only for reward and evaluation)

numbers.eval_set_note: 60 held-out test scenes, 200m x 200m maps, 3 seeds, 3 random initial positions
numbers.evidence: Tab. 1 main results (DINOv3); Tab. 6 additional metrics
Tab. 1 main results (CLIP); additional metrics table

numbers.eval_set_note: real-world UrbanBIS reconstructed mesh, direct sim-to-real transfer without fine-tuning; CCR reported on car and building only
numbers.backbone: ResNet policy trained in simulator + DINOv3

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark; metrics are coverage/classification of the semantic map, not SR/SPL.
results: On the new urban dataset the method achieves OCR 97.1 (DINOv3) and 94.9 (CLIP) with the lowest variance across scales, beating GLEAM (91.7 and 90.0 OCR), the strongest baseline, with the largest gain on small objects (93.2 vs 82.8). It also transfers to real UrbanBIS (OCR 83.5 vs GLEAM 77.1) and runs at 27.39 ms/step.
limitations: Only static scenes are handled; dynamic objects are left for future work.
The dataset is fully simulated, and the real-world check uses a distorted photo-reconstructed mesh with only two classes.
The mapping is 2D and depends on the quality of the frozen VLM; the MI weight k is sensitive (0.2 degrades).
builds_on: Zhang et al. active semantic mapping (Bayesian update)
